passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Polycarp was instructed by apostles, conversed with many who had seen Christ, and was appointed bishop of Smyrna by apostles in Asia; Irenaeus saw him in his early youth. object_entity.notes: Roman presbyter and theologian; prolific Greek-speaking writer in Rome; opposed the modalism of Zephyrinus and Callistus; set himself up as rival bishop c. 217 (sometimes called the first antipope); exiled with Pontian to Sardinia in 235; reconciled before death; author of the Apostolic Tradition, Refutation of All Heresies, Against Noetus, and Commentary on Daniel.

evidence.notes: Hippolytus's Logos theology closely follows Irenaeus; scholarly consensus that Irenaeus was a formative influence.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: God being alone, and having nothing contemporaneous with himself, determined to create the world. He conceived the world in thought and will. He begat the Word, firstborn of all creation, not as a voice but as the internal reckoning of all things. This was the companion of the Father. The Word was made manifest and became the Son of God.
passage.notes: Logos doctrine against modalism; Word begotten from the Father as distinct person; anti-modalist Logos theology

object_entity.notes: Bishop of Carthage c. 248–258; major Latin theologian of ecclesiology and sacramental theology; converted c. 246; deeply influenced by Tertullian; key figure in the Novatian controversy (supported Cornelius against Novatian); martyred under Valerian.

evidence.notes: Cyprian is explicitly the author and narrator of Ad Donatum.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: I myself was held in bonds by the innumerable errors of my previous life and did not believe I could be freed from them. But after the stain of former years had been washed away by the aid of the water of new birth, a light from above poured itself upon my heart now cleansed and purified; after the second birth had restored me to a new man by means of the Spirit breathed from heaven, in a marvellous manner what had been doubtful became certain, what had been hidden was revealed.
passage.notes: Cyprian's conversion and baptismal regeneration testimony; Spirit transformation
